elements.element: No MFN / right-to-match obligation binds Customer (no duty to disclose more favourable third-party offers)
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match Vendor to a competing offer before engaging another provider
elements.evidence: "is not required to disclose or match" replaces "must disclose and match"

elements.element: MFN pricing in Customer's favour permitted / not disturbed
elements.evidence: 7.1 pricing protections left intact: "Fees are fixed during the initial term"

elements.element: MFN limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation remains; 7.2 imposes no product-scoped MFN

reasons: The single replacement in 7.2 flips the operative duty so no MFN/right-to-match obligation runs against Customer, fully achieving the locked preferred level.
Change is confined to the offending sentence; 7.1 fee-fixing and no-hidden-charge protections and all other terms are untouched, introducing no undefined term or dangling mechanic.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, comparison carve-outs) are absent, but they are unnecessary because the preferred position (no MFN at all) is achieved; the vestigial lead-in "Before engaging another provider," is harmless surplusage and could optionally be deleted for tidiness.
